review_locator: PMCID:PMC11467947, Molecular mechanisms underlying microglial sensing and phagocytosis in synaptic pruning

limitations_preserved: Function-only receptor edge; preserve GPR56 S4 isoform and exposed presynaptic phosphatidylserine context, developmental brain-region dependence and no claim that all GPR56 functions or splice forms mediate pruning; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

limitations_preserved: Demyelination/remyelination function-only edge; preserve MERTK loss-of-function and mixed CNS-cell context, and do not transfer to traumatic SCI or infer a direct Gas6/MERTK mechanism from this paper.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9941857, The roles of microglia and astrocytes in myelin phagocytosis in the central nervous system; PMCID:PMC6477030, Phagocytosis in the Brain: Homeostasis and Disease

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11162951, Microglia phagocytic mechanisms: Development informing disease; PMCID:PMC6477030, Phagocytosis in the Brain: Homeostasis and Disease

limitations_preserved: Function/pathway edge for the combined TAM context; preserve AXL/MERTK redundancy and the opsonin/phosphatidylserine context, with no claim that Gas6 acts through one receptor exclusively or that this establishes SCI specificity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4012154, CD47 update: a multifaceted actor in the tumour microenvironment; PMCID:PMC9344092, The roles of microglia and astrocytes in phagocytosis and myelination

limitations_preserved: Preserve myelin CD47-SIRPA interaction, serum dependence and microglia/macrophage context; function-only inhibition edge, not a universal CD47 phagocytosis rule or traumatic-SCI receiver claim.

limitations_preserved: Receptor-level functional inhibition inferred from CD200R down-regulation/priming experiments; preserve CD200 ligand-pair and stress/immune-challenge context, with no direct CD200R1 intracellular mechanism or SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9344092, The roles of microglia and astrocytes in phagocytosis and myelination; PMCID:PMC6477030, Phagocytosis in the Brain: Homeostasis and Disease

decision_basis: The reviews identify CD22 as an age-associated negative regulator of microglial phagocytosis whose blockade restores clearance of myelin debris and protein aggregates.
limitations_preserved: Function-only age-associated inhibitory edge; preserve alpha2,6-linked sialic-acid ligand context and aged-brain model, without assigning a universal CD22 mechanism or traumatic-SCI effect.

review_locator: PMID:39265565, Synaptic Pruning by Microglia: Lessons from Genetic Studies in Mice; PMCID:PMC6477030, Phagocytosis in the Brain: Homeostasis and Disease

decision_basis: The reviews identify neuron-derived CX3CL1-CX3CR1 signaling as required for activity-dependent microglial elimination of thalamocortical synapses.
limitations_preserved: Preserve neuron-derived membrane/soluble fractalkine, CX3CR1 dependence and sensory-lesion barrel-cortex context; do not infer traumatic-SCI synapse pruning or a terminal transcription factor.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8183410, Putting the brakes on phagocytosis; PMID:39265565, Synaptic Pruning by Microglia: Lessons from Genetic Studies in Mice
primary_title: CD47 protects synapses from excess microglia-mediated pruning during development
decision_basis: The reviews identify presynaptic CD47-SIRPalpha engagement as a local don’t-eat-me signal that protects developing synapses from excess microglial engulfment.
limitations_preserved: Preserve neuronal/presynaptic CD47-SIRPA interaction, developmental dLGN/retinogeniculate context and local protection semantics; do not infer universal CD47 inhibition or traumatic-SCI relevance.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8541743, Mechanisms governing activity-dependent synaptic pruning in the mammalian CNS; PMCID:PMC5866459, Microglia-mediated synaptic elimination in neuronal development and disease
primary_title: Microglia sculpt postnatal neural circuits in an activity- and complement-dependent manner
decision_basis: The reviews identify C3 tagging and CR3 recognition as a complement-dependent pathway required for microglial engulfment and elimination of developing retinogeniculate synapses.
limitations_preserved: Preserve activated-C3/CR3 complement context and developing visual-system model; function edge does not claim a purified C3-CR3 complex, a universal complement effect or traumatic-SCI relevance.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5866459, Microglia-mediated synaptic elimination in neuronal development and disease; PMCID:PMC8541743, Mechanisms governing activity-dependent synaptic pruning in the mammalian CNS
primary_title: TGF-beta signaling regulates neuronal C1q expression and developmental synaptic refinement
decision_basis: The reviews identify retinal TGF-beta signaling as an upstream regulator of neuronal C1q expression, complement deposition and microglial synaptic refinement.
limitations_preserved: Retinal-neuron TGFBR2-dependent developmental function edge; preserve receptor-cell and visual-system context, and do not infer a specific TGF-beta isoform, direct C1q binding or traumatic-SCI effect.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11467947, Molecular mechanisms underlying microglial sensing and phagocytosis in synaptic pruning; PMCID:PMC9344092, Phagocytic microglia and macrophages in brain injury and repair
primary_title: Distinct roles for BAI1 and TIM-4 in the engulfment of dying neurons by microglia
decision_basis: The reviews identify BAI1 as a phosphatidylserine receptor whose loss produces a specific defect in phagosome formation and cargo transport during microglial removal of dying neurons.
limitations_preserved: Preserve BAI1/ADGRB1 phosphatidylserine-receptor and zebrafish developmental context; BAI1 controls phagosome formation/cargo transport, while the study does not establish a mammalian SCI branch or intracellular relay.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11467947, Molecular mechanisms underlying microglial sensing and phagocytosis in synaptic pruning; PMCID:PMC9344092, Phagocytic microglia and macrophages in brain injury and repair
primary_title: Distinct roles for BAI1 and TIM-4 in the engulfment of dying neurons by microglia
decision_basis: The reviews identify TIM-4 as a phosphatidylserine receptor required for phagosome stabilization during microglial removal of dying neurons.
limitations_preserved: Preserve TIMD4/TIM4 phosphatidylserine-receptor and zebrafish developmental context; combined BAI1/TIM4 activity is required for clearance, and the study does not establish a mammalian SCI branch or intracellular relay.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10729610, Movers and Shakers: Microglial dynamics and modulation of neural networks; PMCID:PMC12500284, Synaptic Pruning by Microglia: Lessons from Genetic Studies in Mice
primary_title: Microglia promote learning-dependent synapse formation through brain-derived neurotrophic factor
decision_basis: The reviews identify microglia-derived BDNF as the factor required for learning-dependent synapse formation through neuronal TrkB signaling.
limitations_preserved: Record microglial BDNF origin and neuronal TrkB-dependent mechanism; preserve motor-learning/cortical context and do not infer a universal BDNF source, SCI effect or terminal transcription factor.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11467947, Molecular mechanisms underlying microglial sensing and phagocytosis in synaptic pruning; PMCID:PMC8183410, Putting the brakes on phagocytosis
primary_title: Loss of microglial SIRPα promotes synaptic pruning in preclinical models of neurodegeneration
decision_basis: The reviews identify microglial SIRPalpha as a don’t-eat-me checkpoint whose loss increases microglial engulfment and synapse loss in development and neurodegeneration models.
limitations_preserved: Preserve microglial SIRPalpha and CD47 checkpoint context, developmental/Alzheimer models and inhibitory function semantics; do not infer a direct new ligand edge, traumatic-SCI effect or terminal-TF mechanism.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4841266, Microglia: Dynamic Mediators of Synapse Development and Plasticity; PMCID:PMC4786684, Microglial P2Y12 is necessary for synaptic plasticity in mouse visual cortex
primary_title: Microglial P2Y12 is necessary for synaptic plasticity in mouse visual cortex
decision_basis: The reviews identify microglial P2Y12 as the purinergic receptor required for activity-dependent microglial synapse engagement and experience-driven cortical plasticity.
limitations_preserved: Preserve ADP/P2Y12 microglial motility and visual-cortex critical-period context; the primary supports synaptic remodeling/plasticity, not a universal pruning mechanism or traumatic-SCI effect.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10729610, Movers and Shakers: Microglial dynamics and modulation of neural networks; PMCID:PMC12500284, Synaptic Pruning by Microglia: Lessons from Genetic Studies in Mice

decision_basis: The reviews identify microglial TWEAK signaling through neuronal Fn14 as a non-phagocytic mechanism that restricts bulbous-spine number during sensory-dependent retinogeniculate refinement.
limitations_preserved: Preserve microglial TWEAK, neuronal Fn14 and non-phagocytic retinogeniculate developmental context; do not infer generic TWEAK phagocytosis, traumatic-SCI relevance or a terminal transcription factor.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3565973, Essential Role of MFG-E8 for Phagocytic Properties of Microglial Cells; PMCID:PMC9344092, Phagocytic microglia and macrophages in brain injury and repair
primary_title: MFG-E8 Regulates Microglial Phagocytosis of Apoptotic Neurons
decision_basis: The reviews identify MFG-E8 as an opsonin that increases recognition and engulfment of phosphatidylserine-exposing apoptotic neuronal targets by microglia.
limitations_preserved: Preserve MFG-E8 phosphatidylserine-opsonin and microglial/apoptotic-neuron context; do not infer a single integrin subunit, traumatic-SCI effect or universal anti-inflammatory outcome.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3565973, Essential Role of MFG-E8 for Phagocytic Properties of Microglial Cells; PMID:39891478, Emerging Roles for MFG-E8 in Synapse Elimination

limitations_preserved: Preserve TGF-beta1, microglial Mfge8 upregulation and apoptotic-cell context; this is a regulatory function edge, not direct TGF-beta1-MFG-E8 binding or traumatic-SCI inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11467947, Molecular mechanisms underlying microglial sensing and phagocytosis in synaptic pruning; PMCID:PMC9778380, The Diverse Role of CUB and Sushi Multiple Domains 1 in Human Diseases
primary_title: CSMD1 regulates brain complement activity and circuit development

limitations_preserved: Preserve neuronal/synaptic CSMD1 complement-regulator context and CR3 dependence; the primary supports an inhibitory pruning-regulator function, not a direct CSMD1-CR3 binding edge or SCI inference.

primary_title: Microglia mediate forgetting via complement-dependent synaptic elimination

review_locator: PMCID:PMC12500284, Synaptic Pruning by Microglia: Lessons from Genetic Studies in Mice; PMCID:PMC8003660, Microglial Pruning: Relevance for Synaptic Dysfunction in Multiple Sclerosis and Related Experimental Models

primary_title: The classical complement cascade mediates CNS synapse elimination

primary_title: The endogenous neuronal complement inhibitor SRPX2 protects against complement-mediated synapse elimination during development

primary_title: The neuronal pentraxin Nptx2 regulates complement activity and restrains microglia-mediated synapse loss in neurodegeneration
decision_basis: The reviews identify neuronal NPTX2 as a C1q-binding complement regulator whose loss increases complement-dependent microglial synapse engulfment and whose overexpression restrains synapse loss.
limitations_preserved: Preserve neuronal NPTX2-C1q interaction and adult neurodegeneration/FTD context; the primary supports complement regulation and functional restraint, not a direct microglial NPTX2 receptor or SCI inference.

primary_title: Perivascular cells induce microglial phagocytic states and synaptic engulfment via SPP1 in mouse models of Alzheimer's disease

limitations_preserved: Preserve perivascular SPP1 source, oligomeric-Aβ/Alzheimer-model context and receptor-mechanism uncertainty; do not assign a specific integrin/CD44 receptor or SCI transfer.

limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocyte-specific MEGF10 phagocytic function and developmental/retinogeniculate context; do not infer a microglial receptor relay or traumatic-SCI mechanism.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8541743, Mechanisms governing activity-dependent synaptic pruning in the developing mammalian CNS; PMID:38346858, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination
primary_title: Astrocytes mediate synapse elimination through MEGF10 and MERTK pathways
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocytic MERTK as a phagocytic pathway required for synapse elimination; the primary shows Mertk loss reduces astrocyte synaptosome engulfment and impairs activity-dependent retinogeniculate refinement.
limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocyte-specific MERTK phagocytic function and developmental/retinogeniculate context; do not infer a microglial MERTK mechanism or traumatic-SCI transfer.

primary_title: The disintegrin-like metalloproteinase ADAM10 is involved in constitutive cleavage of CX3CL1 (fractalkine) and regulates CX3CL1-mediated cell-cell adhesion

review_locator: PMCID:PMC12500284, Synaptic Pruning by Microglia: Lessons from Genetic Studies in Mice; PMCID:PMC11467947, Molecular mechanisms underlying microglial sensing and phagocytosis in synaptic pruning
primary_title: P2Y6 Receptor-Dependent Microglial Phagocytosis of Synapses during Development Regulates Synapse Density and Memory

limitations_preserved: Preserve developmental microglial P2Y6 functional context and distinguish synapse phagocytosis from UDP-dependent neuronal phagocytosis; no direct receptor-to-engulfment molecular mechanism or SCI/terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6029679, Phagocytic Roles of Glial Cells in Healthy and Diseased Brains; PMID:37428709, The role of the ATP-Binding Cassette A1 in neurological disorders

limitations_preserved: Preserve GULP1 as an intracellular engulfment adaptor in the ABCA1/MEGF10 pathway; function-only, cultured-astrocyte and ischemic-penumbra context, with no direct receptor or traumatic-SCI inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5797987, A Microglia-Cytokine Axis to Modulate Synaptic Connectivity and Function; PMCID:PMC9124570, Microglia in brain development and regeneration
primary_title: Neuronal synapse formation induced by microglia and interleukin 10

limitations_preserved: Preserve microglia-derived IL-10, neuronal IL-10 receptor and early developmental hippocampal culture context; do not infer a microglial intracellular relay, traumatic-SCI effect or terminal-TF mechanism.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6328295, Developmental roles of microglia: a window into mechanisms of disease; PMCID:PMC9124570, Microglia in brain development and regeneration
primary_title: Layer V cortical neurons require microglial support for survival during postnatal development
decision_basis: The reviews identify microglial IGF1 as trophic support for developing layer V cortical neurons; the primary combines microglial depletion/IGF1 inhibition with rescue and neuronal apoptosis readouts.
limitations_preserved: Preserve microglia-derived IGF1, postnatal layer V cortical neuron and developmental context; functional trophic edge only, with no new SCI, terminal-TF or universal IGF1R mechanism inferred.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6328295, Developmental roles of microglia: a window into mechanisms of disease; PMCID:PMC8476102, Microenvironmental Interactions of Oligodendroglial Cells

limitations_preserved: Preserve CD11c-positive neonatal microglia and developmental primary myelination context; function-only trophic association, not a direct IGF1 receptor-complex or SCI remyelination claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9124570, Microglia in brain development and regeneration; PMCID:PMC8476102, Microenvironmental Interactions of Oligodendroglial Cells

limitations_preserved: Preserve NRP1 on adjacent microglia, PDGF-AA/PDGFRalpha trans-activation and developmental/demyelination context; cross-cell functional relay only, not direct NRP1-OPC binding or traumatic-SCI inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8476102, Microenvironmental Interactions of Oligodendroglial Cells; PMCID:PMC5954071, Activin receptors regulate the oligodendrocyte lineage in health and disease
primary_title: M2 microglia and macrophages drive oligodendrocyte differentiation during CNS remyelination
decision_basis: The reviews identify microglial/macrophage-derived Activin-A as a remyelination cue; the primary shows M2-conditioned media enhances oligodendrocyte differentiation and Activin-A blockade inhibits the response in cerebellar slice cultures.
limitations_preserved: Preserve Activin-A/INHBA, M2 microglia/macrophage conditioned-media and demyelination/remyelination context; bounded functional ligand-to-lineage effect, without selecting an ACVR subtype or inferring SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7055422, Glial Cells: Role of the Immune Response in Ischemic Stroke; PMCID:PMC8305833, Glial Cells as Therapeutic Approaches in Brain Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury
primary_title: The interleukin-4/PPARgamma signaling axis promotes oligodendrocyte differentiation and remyelination after brain injury
decision_basis: The reviews identify IL-4 as a repair-associated cytokine in ischemic white-matter injury and trace the effect to the cited primary study; the primary shows IL-4 receptor expression in glial and oligodendrocyte-lineage cells, IL-4 deficiency worsening white-matter injury, and receptor-dependent OPC differentiation/remyelination with an OPC-specific PPARgamma boundary.
limitations_preserved: Preserve IL-4/IL-4 receptor-alpha context and direct OPC effect; PPARgamma is a mechanistic intracellular mediator, not promoted as a terminal-TF edge; stroke/demyelination context only, with no traumatic-SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8305833, Glial Cells as Therapeutic Approaches in Brain Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury; PMID:33970426, Therapeutic Potential of Cytokines in Demyelinating Lesions After Stroke
primary_title: TGFalpha preserves oligodendrocyte lineage cells and improves white matter integrity after cerebral ischemia
decision_basis: The reviews identify TGF-alpha as an oligodendrocyte-protective EGF-family factor after ischemic injury and cite the primary study; the primary shows TGF-alpha induction in microglia/macrophages and neurons, increased EGFR in glial/oligodendrocyte-lineage cells, TGF-alpha knockout worsening OPC/oligodendrocyte death and white-matter loss, and direct protection in OGD cultures.
limitations_preserved: Preserve TGF-alpha-to-EGFR and oligodendrocyte-lineage protection context; the primary supports protection but not differentiation, and STAT3 remains a downstream mediator rather than a promoted terminal-TF edge; ischemic-stroke context only.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4569526, Mechanisms of cell-cell interaction in oligodendrogenesis and remyelination after stroke; PMCID:PMC7055422, Glial Cells: Role of the Immune Response in Ischemic Stroke
primary_title: CXCL12 Gene Therapy Ameliorates Ischemia-Induced White Matter Injury in Mouse Brain
decision_basis: The reviews identify CXCL12/CXCR4 signaling as a regulator of OPC responses after ischemic white-matter injury and cite the gene-therapy study; the primary shows delayed CXCL12 gene delivery improves myelin integrity and increases CXCR4-dependent OPC proliferation and migration, with AMD3100 blockade eliminating the benefit.
limitations_preserved: Preserve CXCL12/CXCR4 dependence, delayed gene-delivery and adult ischemic-stroke context; this is a functional repair edge, not a new direct CXCL12-OPC binding claim or traumatic-SCI inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4545468, The axon-glia unit in white matter stroke: mechanisms of damage and recovery; PMCID:PMC4569526, Mechanisms of cell-cell interaction in oligodendrogenesis and remyelination after stroke
primary_title: Netrin-1 overexpression promotes white matter repairing and remodeling after focal cerebral ischemia in mice
decision_basis: The reviews identify Netrin-1 as a repair-associated guidance factor in ischemic white-matter remodeling and cite the focal-ischemia overexpression study; the primary shows AAV-Netrin-1 increases OPC proliferation, oligodendrocyte maturation and remyelination with improved neurological outcomes.
limitations_preserved: Preserve AAV-Netrin-1 overexpression and focal-cerebral-ischemia context; receptor-specific mechanisms are not promoted beyond the primary perturbation, and no traumatic-SCI or terminal-TF inference is made.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4861901, Astrocytes in Oligodendrocyte Lineage Development and White Matter Pathology; PMCID:PMC2601644, Growth factor regulation of remyelination
primary_title: Platelet-derived growth factor promotes repair of chronically demyelinated white matter
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocyte-derived PDGF-A as a regulator of oligodendrocyte-lineage repair and trace the chronic-demyelination result to the cited primary; the primary shows astrocyte-promoter-driven PDGF-A increases oligodendrocyte density and remyelination and reduces oligodendrocyte-lineage apoptosis after chronic cuprizone demyelination.
limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocyte-derived PDGF-A, chronic cuprizone white-matter context and functional remyelination layer; the primary leaves the precise survival mechanism unresolved, so no extra adaptor or terminal-TF edge is inferred.

review_locator: PMID:31616249, Central Nervous System Remyelination: Roles of Glia and Innate Immune Cells; PMCID:PMC4861901, Astrocytes in Oligodendrocyte Lineage Development and White Matter Pathology
primary_title: Astrocyte-derived endothelin-1 inhibits remyelination through Notch activation
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocyte-derived endothelin-1 as an upstream regulator of Jagged1 during remyelination and cite the primary study; the primary shows endothelin-1 induces Jagged1 in cultured astrocytes and demyelinated lesions, while endothelin antagonism or astrocyte-specific endothelin-1 loss reduces Jagged1 and Notch activation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve reactive-astrocyte and demyelination-lesion context; this is an upstream expression/function edge, not direct EDN1-JAG1 binding and not a new terminal-TF or SCI claim.

review_locator: PMID:31616249, Central Nervous System Remyelination: Roles of Glia and Innate Immune Cells; PMCID:PMC4861901, Astrocytes in Oligodendrocyte Lineage Development and White Matter Pathology
primary_title: Endothelin-B receptor activation in astrocytes regulates the rate of oligodendrocyte regeneration during remyelination
decision_basis: The reviews describe selective EDNRB signaling in astrocytes as the receptor branch that controls the remyelination inhibitor program; the primary uses pharmacological and cell-specific receptor ablation to show endothelin signaling through EDNRB in astrocytes regulates the remyelination rate and the associated Jagged1/Notch pathway.
limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocyte EDNRB and endothelin/Jagged1/Notch remyelination context; the primary supports receptor-mediated functional regulation rather than direct receptor-JAG1 binding, with no traumatic-SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMID:31616249, Central Nervous System Remyelination: Roles of Glia and Innate Immune Cells; PMCID:PMC4569526, Mechanisms of cell-cell interaction in oligodendrogenesis and remyelination after stroke
primary_title: Astrocyte-derived endothelin-1 inhibits remyelination through Notch activation
decision_basis: The reviews identify endothelin-1 as an endogenous remyelination inhibitor and trace the claim to the primary study; gain- and loss-of-function experiments show endothelin-1 reduces OPC differentiation and remyelination, whereas receptor antagonism accelerates repair through reduced Notch activation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocyte-derived endothelin-1, Jagged1/Notch intermediary and LPC demyelination context; no claim of direct EDN1-OPC binding or traumatic-SCI mechanism.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination; PMCID:PMC7600026, Astrocytic Factors Controlling Synaptogenesis: A Team Play
primary_title: Astrocyte-secreted chordin like 1 drives synapse maturation and limits plasticity by increasing synaptic GluA2 AMPA receptors
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocyte-secreted CHRDL1 as a synapse-maturation factor and cite the primary; purified CHRDL1 increases GluA2 surface clustering and functional synapses in rat retinal ganglion-cell cultures, immunodepletion removes astrocyte-conditioned-medium activity, and Chrdl1 loss reduces synaptic GluA2 in mouse cortex.
limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocyte-secreted CHRDL1, GluA2/synapse-maturation outcome and developmental visual-cortex/RGC context; mechanism is reported BMP-independent and no receptor or SCI/terminal-TF edge is inferred.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination; PMCID:PMC7600026, Astrocytic Factors Controlling Synaptogenesis: A Team Play
primary_title: Control of excitatory CNS synaptogenesis by astrocyte-secreted proteins Hevin and SPARC
decision_basis: The reviews identify SPARC as an astrocyte-secreted antagonist of hevin synaptogenesis and cite the primary; recombinant SPARC blocks hevin-induced synapse formation in rat retinal ganglion-cell cultures, while Sparc-null mice show increased retinocollicular synaptic connections.
limitations_preserved: Preserve SPARC antagonism of hevin-dependent excitatory synaptogenesis and superior-colliculus/RGC context; primary does not establish a direct SPARC-hevin complex or a specific neuronal receptor, so no binding mechanism or SCI inference is added.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11662987, Microglia and Astrocytes in Postnatal Neural Circuit Formation; PMID:38346858, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination
primary_title: Astrocyte-secreted neurocan controls inhibitory synapse formation and function
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocyte-secreted Neurocan as a circuit-specific inhibitory synaptogenic factor and trace the claim to the primary; Neurocan C-terminal loss reduces somatostatin-positive inhibitory synapses and mIPSC function, while purified/application and genetic assays support the synaptogenic effect.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the secreted, proteolytically cleaved Neurocan C-terminal fragment and SST-positive cortical inhibitory-synapse context; the primary does not resolve a specific neuronal receptor, so no receptor-binding or SCI inference is added.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7600026, Astrocytic Factors Controlling Synaptogenesis: A Team Play; PMCID:PMC5573249, Molecular Mechanisms of Astrocyte-Induced Synaptogenesis
primary_title: SPARC triggers a cell-autonomous program of synapse elimination
decision_basis: The reviews describe SPARC as a glial trigger of synapse elimination and cite the primary; full-length SPARC or its active C-terminal p4.2 peptide induces concentration- and time-dependent cholinergic synapse disassembly in autaptic cultures, and p4.2 causes transient neuromuscular-junction loss in Xenopus tropicalis tadpoles.
limitations_preserved: Preserve glial SPARC and its C-terminal p4.2 activity, cholinergic developmental-remodeling context and transient Xenopus phenotype; no specific neuronal receptor, intracellular relay or SCI inference is added.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8387342, Cell adhesion molecules regulating astrocyte-neuron interactions; PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination
primary_title: Chemico-genetic discovery of astrocytic control of inhibition in vivo
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocytic NRCAM as a regulator of inhibitory astrocyte-neuron contacts and trace the claim to the primary; astrocyte-specific or neuronal NrCAM depletion reduces inhibitory synapse number and function, while co-culture/rescue assays support a transcellular NRCAM-linked, gephyrin-dependent mechanism.
limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocytic versus neuronal NRCAM and gephyrin-linked transcellular context; primary supports function and transcellular association but not a purified direct ligand-receptor binding assay, so no new binary receptor edge or SCI/terminal-TF inference is added.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination; PMCID:PMC8387342, Cell adhesion molecules regulating astrocyte-neuron interactions
primary_title: HepaCAM controls astrocyte self-organization and coupling
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocytic HepaCAM as a regulator of inhibitory synapse organization and function and trace the claim to the primary; astrocyte-specific Hepacam deletion reduces inhibitory synapse density and mIPSC strength while increasing excitatory synaptic strength in developing mouse cortex.
limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocytic HepaCAM and developmental cortical context; the primary leaves a direct neuronal homophilic mechanism unresolved, so encode function-only with no binary binding, SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2650399, Gap junctions couple astrocytes and oligodendrocytes; PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination
primary_title: Two distinct heterotypic channels mediate gap junction coupling between astrocyte and oligodendrocyte connexins
decision_basis: The reviews identify Cx47/Cx43 as an astrocyte-oligodendrocyte channel and trace the claim to the primary; paired connexin systems show functional heterotypic channels by electrophysiology, immunocytochemistry and dye-permeability assays.
limitations_preserved: Preserve Cx47/GJC2 oligodendrocyte and Cx43/GJA1 astrocyte pairing and heterotypic channel scope; this supports channel assembly/function in expression systems, not a generic myelination or traumatic-SCI edge.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2650399, Gap junctions couple astrocytes and oligodendrocytes; PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination
primary_title: Two distinct heterotypic channels mediate gap junction coupling between astrocyte and oligodendrocyte connexins
decision_basis: The reviews identify Cx32/Cx30 as an astrocyte-oligodendrocyte channel and trace the claim to the primary; paired connexin systems show functional heterotypic channels by electrophysiology, immunocytochemistry and dye-permeability assays.
limitations_preserved: Preserve Cx32/GJB1 oligodendrocyte and Cx30/GJB6 astrocyte pairing and heterotypic channel scope; this supports channel assembly/function in expression systems, not a generic myelination or traumatic-SCI edge.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5573249, Molecular Mechanisms of Astrocyte-Induced Synaptogenesis; PMCID:PMC8284252, Astrocyte-Neuron Signaling in Synaptogenesis
primary_title: Astrocyte-induced Synaptogenesis Is Mediated by Transforming Growth Factor beta Signaling through Modulation of d-Serine Levels in Cerebral Cortex Neurons
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocyte-associated TGF-beta1 as an excitatory synaptogenic factor and trace the claim to the primary; astrocyte-conditioned medium and purified TGF-beta1 increase cortical synaptic puncta, while TGF-beta-pathway inhibition, NMDA-receptor blockade and disruption of D-serine signaling suppress the effect.
limitations_preserved: Preserve TGF-beta1 form, cortical astrocyte/neuron context and D-serine/NMDA-receptor-dependent synaptogenic mechanism; the primary does not isolate a specific TGFBR subunit or establish a traumatic-SCI effect.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5573249, Molecular Mechanisms of Astrocyte-Induced Synaptogenesis; PMCID:PMC11662987, Microglia and Astrocytes in Postnatal Neural Circuit Formation
primary_title: Astrocyte transforming growth factor beta 1 promotes inhibitory synapse formation via CaM kinase II signaling
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocyte-associated TGF-beta1 as an inhibitory synaptogenic factor and trace the claim to the primary; human and murine astrocyte-conditioned medium and purified TGF-beta1 increase cortical inhibitory synapses, pathway manipulation blocks the effect, and CaMKII-dependent Neuroligin-2 clustering is implicated in vitro and in vivo.
limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocyte-conditioned-medium/purified TGF-beta1, cortical inhibitory-synapse and CaMKII/Neuroligin-2 context; the primary does not isolate a specific receptor subunit and later review discussion notes uncertainty about astrocytic versus microglial TGF-beta1 in vivo.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5573249, Molecular Mechanisms of Astrocyte-Induced Synaptogenesis; PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination
primary_title: Astrocyte glypicans 4 and 6 promote formation of excitatory synapses via GluA1 AMPA receptors
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocyte-derived glypicans 4 and 6 as sufficient to induce functional excitatory synapses and to increase postsynaptic AMPAR recruitment, tracing the claim to Allen et al.; the primary identifies GPC6 in the active astrocyte-conditioned-medium signal and shows GPC4/6 depletion reduces induced postsynaptic activity and GluA1 clustering.
limitations_preserved: Preserve GPC4/6 family-signal and astrocyte-conditioned-medium context; the primary isolates direct purified-factor application most clearly for GPC4 and uses combined GPC4/6 depletion, so do not claim GPC6-exclusive GluA1 sufficiency or a specific neuronal receptor.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2718351, Glial ephrin-A3 regulates hippocampal dendritic spine morphology and glutamate transport; PMCID:PMC8387342, Cell adhesion molecules regulating astrocyte-neuron interactions
primary_title: Control of hippocampal dendritic spine morphology through ephrin-A3/EphA4 signaling
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocytic ephrin-A3 as the EphA4 ligand that controls dendritic spine morphology and trace the claim to Murai et al.; ephrin-A3 localized to astrocytic processes activates neuronal EphA4, causing spine retraction, while blocking the interaction or EphA4 loss disrupts spine organization.
limitations_preserved: Preserve astrocyte-to-neuron contact, GPI-anchored ephrin-A3 and EphA4 forward-signaling context; no generalized EphA4 downstream relay, SCI transfer or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3922060, Neuron-glia communication via EphA4/ephrinA3 modulates LTP through glial glutamate transport; PMCID:PMC8387342, Cell adhesion molecules regulating astrocyte-neuron interactions
primary_title: Ephrin-A3 reverse signaling regulates hippocampal neuronal damage and astrocytic glutamate transport after transient global ischemia
decision_basis: The reviews trace astrocytic ephrin-A3 reverse signaling by neuronal EphA4 to regulation of glial glutamate transport; ephrin-A3 loss or EphA4 loss increases GLAST/GLT-1, astrocytic ephrin-A3 overexpression lowers transporter levels, and transporter inhibition rescues the LTP defect.
limitations_preserved: Encode this as ephrin-A3 reverse-signaling function rather than a direct ephrin-A3-to-transporter interaction; preserve neuronal EphA4/astrocytic ephrin-A3 topology and ischemia/hippocampal context, with no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10269688, Astrocytic modulation of neuronal signalling; PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination
primary_title: Astrocyte-derived small extracellular vesicles promote synapse formation via fibulin-2-mediated TGF-beta signaling
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocyte-derived small extracellular vesicles as a synaptogenic source and trace fibulin-2 to Patel and Weaver; the primary shows recombinant fibulin-2 increases cortical-neuron spines and synapses, increases Smad2 phosphorylation, and loses effect when TGF-beta signaling is inhibited.
limitations_preserved: Keep this as astrocyte-EV/recombinant-fibulin-2 functional evidence with TGF-beta dependence; no direct neuronal receptor is established, the EV cargo is not exclusive to fibulin-2, and no in vivo or SCI claim is inferred.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5643215, Regulation of neural circuit formation by protocadherins; DOI:10.1016/j.neures.2022.09.014, Neuronal and astrocytic protein connections and associated adhesion molecules
primary_title: Control of CNS synapse development by gamma-protocadherin-mediated astrocyte-neuron contact
decision_basis: The reviews identify gamma-protocadherins as astrocyte-expressed perisynaptic adhesion molecules and trace the contact-dependent synaptogenesis claim to Garrett and Weiner; astrocyte-neuron gamma-Pcdh contacts are required for developing-culture synaptogenesis, and astrocyte-restricted mutation delays both excitatory and inhibitory synapse formation in vivo.
limitations_preserved: Encode a contact-dependent functional family edge rather than a single gamma-Pcdh isoform or direct binary receptor pair; preserve astrocytic expression, developmental context, and no SCI/terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: DOI:10.1016/j.neures.2022.09.014, Neuronal and astrocytic protein connections and associated adhesion molecules; PMCID:PMC12081453, Exploring perspectives of Dscam for cognitive deficits
primary_title: Neuronal DSCAM regulates the peri-synaptic localization of GLAST in Bergmann glia for functional synapse formation
decision_basis: The reviews identify the neuron-astrocyte DSCAM-GLAST mechanism and cite Dewa et al.; the primary reports an intercellular association between neuronal DSCAM and astrocytic GLAST, loss of GLAST peri-synaptic localization and glutamate clearance in Dscam mutants, and rescue of proximal synapse-formation impairment by GLAST activation.
limitations_preserved: Treat this as an intercellular neuron-to-astrocyte protein association with functional transporter/synapse consequences, not a classical secreted ligand-receptor edge; preserve Bergmann-glia/Purkinje-cell context and no SCI/terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC12162199, Developmental roles of astrocytes in circuit wiring; PMCID:PMC10269688, Astrocytic modulation of neuronal signalling
primary_title: Aberrant astrocyte protein secretion contributes to altered neuronal development in multiple models of neurodevelopmental disorders
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocyte-secreted IGFBP2 as an inhibitor of IGF-dependent neuronal growth and trace the claim to Caldwell et al.; the primary finds increased astrocyte Igfbp2 in neurodevelopmental-disorder models, partial rescue by Igfbp2 blockade, and reversal of astrocyte-mediated neurite-outgrowth inhibition when upstream BMP signaling is blocked.
limitations_preserved: Keep this as disease-model astrocyte-secretome functional inhibition of IGF-dependent neuronal development; the primary supports contribution rather than an isolated universal mechanism, and no direct neuronal receptor or SCI claim is inferred.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9255715, Adhesion G protein-coupled receptors: structure, signaling, physiology, and pathophysiology; PMCID:PMC4736325, Emerging Roles of BAI Adhesion-GPCRs in Synapse Development and Plasticity
primary_title: C1QL3 promotes cell-cell adhesion by mediating complex formation between ADGRB3/BAI3 and neuronal pentraxins
decision_basis: The reviews identify NPTX1 as a neuronal-pentraxin component of the C1QL3-ADGRB3 trans-synaptic adhesion complex and trace the claim to Sticco et al.; the primary demonstrates bona fide C1QL3-NPTX1 binding by cell-surface assays, pulldown and SPR, with low-micromolar affinities, and shows that C1QL3 can simultaneously organize NPTX1 and ADGRB3 into a cell-cell adhesion complex.
limitations_preserved: Promote only the direct C1QL3-NPTX1 binding/complex layer; preserve oligomeric C1QL3, low-micromolar multivalent SPR kinetics, cortical neuronal adhesion context and simultaneous ADGRB3/NPTX1 complex topology. Do not promote C1QL3-NPTXR as an equivalent edge, infer a generalized C1QL family interaction or SCI function, or add terminal-TF claims.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4286395, Canonical and non-canonical Notch ligands; PMCID:PMC2613471, Revisiting Notch in remyelination of multiple sclerosis lesions
primary_title: F3/contactin acts as a functional ligand for Notch during oligodendrocyte maturation
decision_basis: The reviews identify F3/contactin as a GPI-linked non-canonical Notch ligand and trace the claim to Hu et al.; the primary reports contactin-Notch interaction, gamma-secretase-dependent NICD generation and Deltex-associated oligodendrocyte maturation/MAG induction in OL models.
limitations_preserved: Promote at the exact F3/contactin-NOTCH1 non-canonical ligand/activation and oligodendrocyte-maturation layer; preserve GPI-linked contactin, gamma-secretase/Deltex dependence, Notch1/Notch2 comparator semantics, and no generalized canonical Notch or SCI claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4286395, Canonical and non-canonical Notch ligands; PMCID:PMC8424196, Functions and Molecular Mechanisms of Deltex Family Ubiquitin E3 Ligases in Development and Disease
primary_title: NB-3/Notch1 pathway via Deltex1 promotes neural progenitor cell differentiation into oligodendrocytes
decision_basis: The reviews identify NB-3/contactin-6 as a non-canonical Notch1 ligand and trace the claim to Cui et al.; the primary reports NB-3-dependent Notch1 NICD nuclear translocation, Deltex1-dependent oligodendrogliogenesis and increased MAG transcripts in primary oligodendrocytes.
limitations_preserved: Promote at the exact NB-3/contactin-6-NOTCH1 non-canonical ligand/activation and oligodendrocyte-differentiation layer; preserve gamma-secretase/NICD and Deltex1 dependence, developmental model limits, and no terminal-TF claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9921585, Contactins: structural aspects in relation to developmental functions in brain disease; PMCID:PMC2675151, Contactins: Emerging key roles in the development and function of the nervous system
primary_title: Neural recognition molecules CHL1 and NB-3 regulate apical dendrite orientation in the neocortex via PTPalpha
decision_basis: The reviews identify CHL1 and NB-3/contactin-6 as a cis-interacting neural adhesion pair and trace the claim to Ye et al.; the primary demonstrates direct association, co-localization and CHL1-dependent enhancement of NB-3 surface expression in transfected cells and cortical neurons, with compound-loss developmental phenotypes.
limitations_preserved: Promote only the CHL1-NB-3/contactin-6 cis-association and surface-expression layer; preserve neuronal developmental context, direct-association versus trans-ligand boundary, and no unsupported receptor activation or SCI claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9921585, Contactins: structural aspects in relation to developmental functions in brain disease; PMCID:PMC8728108, Interplay in neural functions of cell adhesion molecule close homolog of L1 and Programmed Cell Death 6
primary_title: Neural recognition molecules CHL1 and NB-3 regulate apical dendrite orientation in the neocortex via PTPalpha
decision_basis: The reviews identify PTPRA as a signaling mediator for CHL1 and trace the claim to Ye et al.; the primary demonstrates CHL1-PTPRA co-immunoprecipitation in HEK293T and mouse brain, PTPRA redistribution to CHL1 clusters, FYN Y531 dephosphorylation and cortical dendrite-orientation dependence.
limitations_preserved: Promote the bounded CHL1-PTPRA receptor-complex association/relay; preserve antibody-clustering, developmental neocortex and FYN dephosphorylation context, and do not infer an isolated phosphatase catalytic mechanism or SCI function.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9921585, Contactins: structural aspects in relation to developmental functions in brain disease; PMCID:PMC2675151, Contactins: Emerging key roles in the development and function of the nervous system
primary_title: Neural recognition molecules CHL1 and NB-3 regulate apical dendrite orientation in the neocortex via PTPalpha
decision_basis: The reviews identify PTPRA as a signaling mediator for NB-3/contactin-6 and trace the claim to Ye et al.; the primary demonstrates NB-3-PTPRA co-immunoprecipitation in HEK293T, PTPRA redistribution to NB-3 clusters, FYN Y531 dephosphorylation and NB-3-dependent cortical dendrite-orientation phenotypes.
limitations_preserved: Promote the bounded NB-3/contactin-6-PTPRA receptor-complex association/relay; preserve heterologous co-IP, antibody-clustering, developmental neocortex and FYN dephosphorylation caveats, and do not claim in-vivo direct binding or SCI function.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8387342, Cell adhesion molecules regulating astrocyte-neuron interactions; PMCID:PMC7339444, Protocadherins at the Crossroad of Signaling Pathways
primary_title: gamma-Protocadherins interact with neuroligin-1 and negatively regulate dendritic spine morphogenesis
decision_basis: The reviews identify gamma-protocadherin cis interaction with neuroligin-1 and trace the claim to Molumby et al.; the primary demonstrates extracellular-domain interaction in co-transfected COS cells and P6 mouse cortex, and shows inhibition of neuroligin-1-dependent presynaptic differentiation and dendritic spine formation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve cis ectodomain interaction, multiple gamma-Pcdh isoforms and inhibition of NLGN1-neurexin synaptogenic signaling; no generalized PCDHG intracellular relay or SCI inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8387342, Cell adhesion molecules regulating astrocyte-neuron interactions; PMCID:PMC7339444, Protocadherins at the Crossroad of Signaling Pathways
primary_title: The gamma-Protocadherins interact physically and functionally with Neuroligin-2 to negatively regulate inhibitory synapse density and are required for normal social interaction
decision_basis: The reviews identify gamma-protocadherin cis interaction with neuroligin-2 and trace the claim to Steffen et al.; the primary demonstrates extracellular-domain interaction in COS cells and forebrain tissue, and shows reduced neuroligin-2-induced presynaptic maturation plus increased inhibitory synapse density after forebrain Pcdhg loss.
limitations_preserved: Preserve cis ectodomain interaction, multiple gamma-Pcdh isoforms and inhibition of NLGN2 synaptogenic activity; no generalized PCDHG intracellular relay or SCI inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6689999, Thy-1/CD90 a Bidirectional and Lateral Signaling Scaffold; PMCID:PMC6397864, Thy-1 in Integrin Mediated Mechanotransduction
primary_title: Neuronal Thy-1 induces astrocyte adhesion by engaging syndecan-4 in a cooperative interaction with alphaVbeta3 integrin that activates PKCalpha and RhoA
decision_basis: The reviews identify neuronal Thy-1/CD90 engagement of astrocytic syndecan-4 as a cooperative receptor interaction with alphaVbeta3 integrin and trace the claim to Avalos et al.; the primary shows dependence on the Thy-1 heparin-binding motif and astrocytic syndecan-4, with PKCalpha/RhoA-dependent adhesion and focal-adhesion responses.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the cooperative Thy-1-SDC4-alphaVbeta3 complex, heparin-binding-domain dependence and astrocyte adhesion/migration context; do not treat SDC4 as an autonomous kinase receptor or infer a universal THY1-SDC4 binary mechanism or SCI transfer.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3058235, Contribution of Glial-Neuronal Interactions to the Neuroendocrine Control of Female Puberty
primary_title: The synaptic cell adhesion molecule SynCAM1 mediates astrocyte-to-astrocyte and astrocyte-to-GnRH neuron adhesiveness; SynCAM1 contributes to erbB4 receptor-mediated control of female sexual development
decision_basis: The review identifies ligand-dependent astroglial ErbB4 association with SynCAM1 and traces the adhesive mechanism to the Sandau primary studies; the primaries show NRGbeta1-dependent ErbB4-SynCAM1 co-immunoprecipitation/direct intracellular-domain interaction and ErbB4-dependent astrocyte-GnRH adhesiveness and developmental reproductive phenotypes.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the NRGbeta1/astrocyte context, direct intracellular association and adhesion/function boundaries; do not infer a general ERBB4 activation edge, autonomous CADM1 signaling, SCI transfer or terminal-TF claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8387342, Cell adhesion molecules regulating astrocyte-neuron interactions; PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination
primary_title: Chemico-genetic discovery of astrocytic control of inhibition in vivo
decision_basis: The reviews identify homophilic NrCAM interaction between astrocytes and neurons as a mechanism controlling astrocyte process growth and inhibitory synapse organization, tracing the claim to Takano et al.; the primary demonstrates cell-type-specific loss/rescue, extracellular-Ig-domain dependence, transcellular co-localization and inhibitory synapse/miniature-IPSC phenotypes.
limitations_preserved: Promote only the bounded homophilic astrocyte-neuron NrCAM adhesion and inhibitory-synapse function; preserve visual-cortex developmental context and no SCI/terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10587848, Neuronal cadherins: The keys that unlock layer-specific astrocyte identity?; PMID:40334496, Cell biology of astrocytic adhesive interactions and signaling pathways in regulating neuronal circuits
primary_title: delta-Catenin controls astrocyte morphogenesis via layer-specific astrocyte-neuron cadherin interactions
decision_basis: The reviews identify astrocytic delta-catenin association with N-cadherin as a mechanism that stabilizes cadherin surface expression and supports neuron-contact-dependent astrocyte morphogenesis; the primary combines structural modeling, biochemical surface-expression assays and astrocyte-neuron perturbation to support this bounded cadherin-catenin mechanism.
limitations_preserved: Promote only the bounded CTNND2/CDH2 adhesion-complex association and neuron-contact-dependent astrocyte morphogenesis; preserve the modeled juxtamembrane interaction, surface-localization and developmental cortical context, with no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8387342, Cell adhesion molecules regulating astrocyte-neuron interactions; PMCID:PMC11293538, Astrocyte Regulation of Synapse Formation, Maturation, and Elimination
