review_locator: PMCID:PMC10417178, EPH/Ephrin Signaling in Normal Hematopoiesis and Hematologic Malignancies; EphA/ephrin-A family and signaling section
primary_title: Ephrin A4-ephrin receptor A10 signaling promotes cell migration and spheroid formation by upregulating NANOG expression in oral squamous cell carcinoma cells
decision_basis: The review provides EphA/ephrin-A receptor-family context and the cited primary directly tests EFNA4-EPHA10 forward signaling; EFNA4-Fc induces ERK activation, migration and sphere formation in EPHA10-positive oral squamous-cell carcinoma cells, with EPHA10 knockdown and ERK inhibition controls.
limitations_preserved: Preserve GPI-anchored ephrin-A4 and the atypical kinase-null EPHA10 forward-signaling/tumor-cell context; the primary supports ligand-induced ERK-dependent function but does not establish a purified complex or generalize to other EphA receptors, CNS/SCI or terminal-TF claims.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7233459, Adhesion protein structure, molecular affinities, and principles of cell-cell recognition; type-I cadherin section
primary_title: Structural and energetic determinants of adhesive binding specificity in type I cadherins
decision_basis: The review describes type-I cadherin trans recognition and cites the primary quantitative study; purified mouse P-cadherin EC1-EC2 fragments self-associate in calcium-dependent analytical-ultracentrifugation assays with a reported homophilic KD of about 30.9 micromolar.
limitations_preserved: Preserve calcium-dependent P-cadherin EC1-EC2 ectodomain self-association and the quantified soluble affinity; this is an adhesion-layer identity, not an intracellular receptor relay or SCI claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7233459, Adhesion protein structure, molecular affinities, and principles of cell-cell recognition; type-I cadherin section
primary_title: Structural and energetic determinants of adhesive binding specificity in type I cadherins
decision_basis: The review cites the primary type-I cadherin specificity study, which measured direct heterophilic P-cadherin/E-cadherin interaction by surface plasmon resonance using purified ectodomains in calcium-containing buffer.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the weak calcium-dependent heterophilic ectodomain interaction and subtype-comparison context; do not infer a unique cellular junction stoichiometry, cytoplasmic relay or SCI function.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11592701, Cell Adhesion Molecules as Modulators of the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor; EGFR regulation by other CAMs section
primary_title: Extracellular domain of EpCAM enhances tumor progression through EGFR signaling in colon cancer cells; EpCAM ectodomain EpEX is a ligand of EGFR in head and neck cancers
decision_basis: The review identifies soluble EpCAM ectodomain EpEX as an EGFR ligand and cites primary studies showing EpEX-EGFR interaction or ligand assignment, EGFR phosphorylation, ERK/AKT activation and receptor-dependent epithelial-cancer-cell outputs.
limitations_preserved: Preserve soluble/cleaved EpEX rather than intact EpCAM, epithelial-cancer-cell context and ligand-dependent EGFR activation; the cited studies do not establish a solved structural complex or SCI/terminal-TF claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11592701, Cell Adhesion Molecules as Modulators of the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor; Ninjurin2/EGFR section
primary_title: Ninjurin2 overexpression promotes glioma cell growth
decision_basis: The review cites the primary glioma study reporting Ninjurin-2 complex formation with EGFR and receptor-associated Akt/ERK dependence; Ninjurin-2 loss suppresses, while overexpression enhances, these outputs in established and primary human glioma cells.
limitations_preserved: Preserve Ninjurin-2/EGFR co-complex and human-glioma context; co-immunoprecipitation supports association and functional dependence but not a purified direct ligand-receptor binding interface, and no SCI or terminal-TF inference is made.

review_locator: PMID:20119872, Ninjurin1: a potential adhesion molecule and its role in inflammation and tissue remodeling; adhesion and nerve-repair discussion; PMCID:PMC13093763, NINJ1 family review
primary_title: Mechanism of homophilic binding mediated by ninjurin, a novel widely expressed adhesion molecule; Ninjurin, a novel adhesion molecule that promotes axonal growth
decision_basis: The reviews describe NINJ1 as a nerve-injury-induced cell-surface adhesion molecule and cite primary work localizing its homophilic adhesion domain; the primary studies use aggregation, competitive peptide, mutational and neurite-extension assays.
limitations_preserved: Restrict to the historical NINJ1 homophilic-adhesion/neurite-extension assay layer; preserve the modern topology paradox concerning the N-terminal adhesion motif and do not infer plasma-membrane rupture, intracellular signaling, SCI receiver function or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11216901, Mechanistic insights from inflammasome structures; NINJ1/NINJ2 adhesion section
primary_title: Ninjurin2, a Novel Homophilic Adhesion Molecule, Is Expressed in Mature Sensory and Enteric Neurons and Promotes Neurite Outgrowth
decision_basis: The review identifies NINJ2 as a cell-surface adhesion molecule and cites the primary study showing NINJ2-dependent homophilic aggregation and neurite outgrowth; the primary also tests and excludes NINJ1-NINJ2 heterophilic interaction.
limitations_preserved: Restrict to NINJ2 homophilic adhesion and neurite-outgrowth function; preserve that NINJ2 does not interact heterophilically with NINJ1 in the cited assay and do not infer intracellular signaling, SCI receiver function or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9578707, Identification of orphan ligand-receptor relationships using a cell-based CRISPRa enrichment screening platform (primary discovery article; no separate review lead identified)
primary_title: Identification of orphan ligand-receptor relationships using a cell-based CRISPRa enrichment screening platform
decision_basis: The primary discovery study identifies PTPRA as a GAS1-interacting receptor by CRISPRa enrichment and validates direct extracellular binding by SPR with a measured dissociation constant of approximately 1.13 micromolar, plus binding to full-length PTPRA-expressing K562 cells.
limitations_preserved: Primary-led direct GAS1-PTPRA extracellular binding only; preserve PTPRA ectodomain/full-length receptor assay and do not infer PTPRA phosphatase signaling, RET coupling, CNS/SCI function or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMID:40700020; PMCID:PMC12453587, IGSF10 is a RET antagonist regulating Ewing sarcoma growth and GnRH neuron migration (primary discovery article; no separate review lead identified)
primary_title: IGSF10 is a RET antagonist regulating Ewing sarcoma growth and GnRH neuron migration
decision_basis: The primary study shows IGSF10 binding to RET by receptor-dependent cell binding, RET extracellular-domain co-immunoprecipitation and ITC of RET-binding fragments; IGSF10 also binds GAS1 and facilitates an inhibitory RET-GAS1 complex that suppresses RET-cdc42 signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve IGSF10 as an inhibitory RET ligand/complex organizer with GAS1 co-receptor context; the paper states that full three-way biochemical reconstitution is lacking, so do not claim a solved ternary complex, generic RET activation, SCI function or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC13100127, Clustering and a conformational switch drive activation of the mammalian receptor tyrosine kinase ROS1 (primary discovery article; no separate review lead identified)
primary_title: Clustering and a conformational switch drive activation of the mammalian receptor tyrosine kinase ROS1
decision_basis: The primary structural study identifies NELL2 as a direct ROS1 agonist: BLI measures direct ROS1 extracellular-domain binding, cryo-EM resolves the NELL2-bound receptor, and NELL2 stimulation activates ROS1 in ROS1-expressing cells.
limitations_preserved: Preserve trimeric NELL2, multisite ROS1 extracellular engagement and the human-ligand/murine-receptor model; the 2026 study resolves direct agonism despite earlier binding-only reports, but do not transfer to Drosophila Sevenless/BOSS, SCI function or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC13272722, Research on the role and mechanism of FAT4 in the development and progression of tumor and non-tumor diseases; C4orf48/NICOL1-NELL2 cofactor discussion
primary_title: Ewing sarcoma depends on C4orf48/NICOL, a NELL2 cofactor regulated by Hippo signaling
decision_basis: The review identifies C4orf48/NICOL1 as a NELL2 cofactor and cites the primary study; purified recombinant proteins show direct C4orf48 binding to the NELL2 coiled-coil domain, while conditioned-medium and cell assays show enhanced NELL2 binding and NELL2-dependent Ewing-sarcoma growth signaling.
limitations_preserved: Restrict this to direct extracellular C4orf48/NICOL1-NELL2 cofactor binding and enhancement of NELL2/Robo3-dependent signaling in Ewing-sarcoma models; do not treat C4orf48 as the NELL2 receptor, infer a new intracellular C4orf48 relay, or transfer to SCI or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5626410, Gpr158 mediates osteocalcin's regulation of cognition; receptor-mediated OCN transduction section; PMCID:PMC12055796, Osteocalcin and GPR158: linking bone and brain function
primary_title: Gpr158 mediates osteocalcin's regulation of cognition
decision_basis: The reviews identify GPR158 as the neuronal osteocalcin receptor and cite primary genetic, electrophysiological and molecular evidence: osteocalcin responses in hippocampal neurons and cognition-related outputs are lost or altered with Gpr158 disruption, with IP3 and BDNF readouts.
limitations_preserved: Restrict to receptor-mediated osteocalcin/GPR158 neuronal functional activation supported by genetic and cellular assays; direct biochemical osteocalcin-GPR158 occupancy was not established in this primary, so do not encode direct binding, infer a universal G-protein mechanism, or transfer to SCI/terminal-TF output.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC9190282, LGR4, a G Protein-Coupled Receptor With a Systemic Role; LGR4 ligands and associated signaling pathways
primary_title: Nidogen-2 is a Novel Endogenous Ligand of LGR4 to Inhibit Vascular Calcification
decision_basis: The review identifies nidogen-2 as an endogenous LGR4 ligand and cites the primary study; nidogen-2 directly binds LGR4 by co-immunoprecipitation, receptor-selective cell binding and SPR, and biased LGR4-Gαq-PKCα-AMPKα1 signaling inhibits vascular smooth-muscle-cell calcification.
limitations_preserved: Preserve NID2 as a basement-membrane ligand and LGR4/GPR48 as the receptor, including the biased Gαq branch and vascular smooth-muscle/calcification context; do not transfer to R-spondin/Norrin/RANKL branches, SCI, or terminal-TF output.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC12869241, Revealing the multiple faces of LRG1: gene expression, structure, function, and therapeutic potential; HER3 section
primary_title: Leucine-Rich Alpha-2-Glycoprotein 1 Promotes Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Growth Through Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 3 Signaling
decision_basis: The review identifies LRG1 as a direct noncanonical HER3 ligand and cites Rathore et al.; the primary demonstrates LRG1 binding to and activation of HER3 distinct from neuregulin, with a downstream PI3K-PDK1-RSK-eIF4B protein-synthesis axis and blockade-sensitive metastatic colorectal-cancer growth.
limitations_preserved: Preserve LRG1 as an alternative/noncanonical HER3 ligand distinct from NRG1, the endothelial-to-CRC liver-metastasis context, direct binding/activation and the PI3K-PDK1-RSK-eIF4B axis; do not assume ERBB2 heterodimerization, canonical NRG signaling, generic ERBB3 universality, SCI effects or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC13192284, Approaches to deorphanize secretome: Classical, computational, and next generation strategies to reveal ligand-receptor networks; GPR50 deorphanization example
primary_title: Photo-cross-linking-assisted deorphanization deciphers GPR50-L-LEN pairing in metabolism
decision_basis: The review identifies Little-LEN as an endogenous GPR50 ligand and cites the primary deorphanization study; photo-crosslinking/MS, competitive ligand binding and receptor-selective assays support physical L-LEN-GPR50 interaction, while GPR50-dependent Gαi signaling, neuronal activity changes and ligand/receptor loss-of-function support bounded metabolic function.
limitations_preserved: Preserve mature Little-LEN/L-LEN peptide form, GPR50 specificity, dominant Gαi/cAMP-inhibition branch and hypothalamus-to-adipose metabolic context; do not generalize to ProSAAS products or GPR171/B-LEN, infer universal GPCR coupling, SCI effects or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC13494238, IUPHAR/BPS objective evaluation of class A orphan GPCRs; GPRC5B section
primary_title: Virion display reveals MD-1 as an endogenous agonist for the orphan receptor GPRC5B
decision_basis: The review cites the primary virion-display deorphanization study reporting MD-1 as a selective endogenous agonist for GPRC5B; receptor-display/proteome-array discovery, adipocyte binding and Gαs-dependent signaling support MD-1-GPRC5B activation, while macrophage-adipocyte contact and receptor-dependent assays support bounded lipolysis function.
limitations_preserved: Preserve MD-1 as a macrophage-derived glycoprotein ligand, GPRC5B specificity, adipocyte Gαs/lipolysis and macrophage-contact context; do not infer a universal GPRC5-family ligand, constitutive signaling, SCI effects or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC12961821, Role of mucosal chemokines in the development of tissue-resident CD4+ and CD8+ TRM cells to fend off herpes simplex infections; CXCL17/GPR25 section
primary_title: Identification of orphan GPR25 as a receptor for the chemokine CXCL17
decision_basis: The review identifies GPR25 as the recently validated CXCL17 receptor and cites the primary FEBS study; recombinant CXCL17 activates GPR25-dependent TGFα shedding and chemotaxis, with ligand C-terminal truncation and receptor-pocket mutations defining a bounded activation interface.
limitations_preserved: Preserve CXCL17 C-terminal ligand form and GPR25 pocket-dependent activation, with heterologous human-cell chemotaxis/shedding context; distinguish GPR25 from the disputed CXCR4/GPR35 reports and do not infer universal chemokine-family behavior, SCI effects or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC13095406, ProSAAS neuropeptides and receptors GPR171 and GPR83: Potential therapeutic applications for pain, anxiety, and body weight regulation; FAM237A/FAM237B section
primary_title: FAM237A, rather than peptide PEN and proCCK56-63, binds to and activates the orphan receptor GPR83
decision_basis: The review identifies FAM237A as a GPR83 ligand and cites the primary validation; mature FAM237A binds human GPR83 with nanomolar affinity in NanoBiT and fluorescent-ligand assays and activates receptor β-arrestin recruitment/internalization in transfected human cells.
limitations_preserved: Preserve mature processed FAM237A protein, GPR83 specificity and heterologous human-cell binding/β-arrestin context; do not transfer PEN/proCCK claims, assume FAM237B equivalence, infer universal GPR83 coupling, SCI effects or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC13095406, ProSAAS neuropeptides and receptors GPR171 and GPR83: Potential therapeutic applications for pain, anxiety, and body weight regulation; FAM237A/FAM237B section
primary_title: A Pilot Screen of a Novel Peptide Hormone Library Identified Candidate GPR83 Ligands
decision_basis: The review identifies the related FAM237B protein as a lower-potency GPR83 activator and cites the primary peptide-hormone-library study; processed FAM237B expression product activates GPR83 in a receptor-screening system.
limitations_preserved: Restrict to lower-potency processed FAM237B-dependent GPR83 activation reported in the primary screening system; direct FAM237B-GPR83 occupancy and in-vivo physiology were not established, so do not encode direct binding, assume FAM237A-equivalent affinity, infer SCI effects or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC13095406, ProSAAS neuropeptides and receptors GPR171 and GPR83: Potential therapeutic applications for pain, anxiety, and body weight regulation; GPR171 section
primary_title: GPR171 is a hypothalamic G protein-coupled receptor for BigLEN, a neuropeptide involved in feeding
decision_basis: The review identifies BigLEN as the endogenous GPR171 ligand and cites the primary deorphanization study; ligand-binding and receptor-activity assays, receptor gain/loss of function, and hypothalamic knockdown support a BigLEN-GPR171 feeding/metabolism axis.
limitations_preserved: Preserve mature BigLEN rather than LittleLEN, GPR171 specificity, the Gαi/o and hypothalamic feeding/metabolism context; do not generalize to GPR83/PEN or GPR50/L-LEN, universal coupling, SCI effects or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11763455, Metabolite-Sensing Receptors: Emerging Targets for Modulating Chronic Pain Pathways; GPR3/OEA section
primary_title: Structural and functional characterization of the endogenous agonist for orphan receptor GPR3
decision_basis: The review identifies OEA as a GPR3-interacting endogenous agonist candidate and cites the primary structural/functional study; OEA is enriched in the GPR3-Gs complex, directly interacts by SPR, increases purified-receptor GTP turnover and activates GPR3 cAMP signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve OEA as the tested GPR3 agonist candidate and distinguish it from oleic acid and oleamide; retain constitutive-activity, purified-receptor and heterologous cAMP assay boundaries, with no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11749842, Cholesin, a new hormone bridges intestinal cholesterol absorption and hepatic synthesis; Cholesin-GPR146 section; PMCID:PMC12508344, Cholesterol metabolism: molecular mechanisms, biological functions, diseases, and therapeutic targets; Cholesin and GPR146 section
primary_title: A gut-derived hormone regulates cholesterol metabolism
decision_basis: The reviews identify Cholesin as a gut-derived GPR146 ligand and cite the primary discovery study; Cholesin binds GPR146 and inhibits the GPR146-associated PKA/ERK1/2 axis, reducing hepatic cholesterol synthesis in receptor-dependent models.
limitations_preserved: Preserve secreted Cholesin/C7orf50, GPR146 and the inhibitory hepatic cholesterol-homeostasis context; direct receptor interface and complete G-protein mechanism remain bounded, and no SCI or terminal-TF inference is made.

review_locator: PMID:38590871, The role of orphan G protein-coupled receptors in pain; GPR37L1/MaR1 section
primary_title: Satellite glial GPR37L1 and its ligand maresin 1 regulate potassium channel signaling and pain homeostasis
decision_basis: The review identifies MaR1 as a GPR37L1 ligand and cites the primary JCI study; MaR1-specific lipid-overlay and protein-pull-down binding, receptor-dependent potassium-channel regulation and neuropathic-pain rescue support a bounded MaR1-GPR37L1 glial signaling axis.
limitations_preserved: Preserve MaR1 stereochemistry and lipid-overlay/pull-down rather than purified-affinity semantics; preserve GPR37L1, satellite-glial DRG and KCNJ10/KCNJ3 context; peripheral neuropathy is not SCI, and no terminal-TF inference is made.

review_locator: PMID:42386506, Peripheral κ opioid receptor in pain and inflammation: From molecular signalling and gene expression to drug discovery; GPR139/dynorphin discussion and Figure 1
primary_title: Homeostatic scaling of dynorphin signaling by a non-canonical opioid receptor
decision_basis: The review identifies GPR139 as a recently deorphanized non-canonical dynorphin receptor and cites the primary study; a custom neuropeptide screen, orthogonal calcium assays, radioligand competition and FITC-dynorphin binding, receptor-selective antagonism, and Gpr139-dependent medial-habenula responses support a bounded PDYN-dynorphin-GPR139 axis.
limitations_preserved: Preserve PDYN-derived dynorphin peptide series and naloxone-insensitive GPR139 binding/activation, with Gαq/11-Ca2+ and medial-habenula neuronal context; do not collapse this edge into OPRK1/KOR, infer a universal dynorphin receptor, transfer to SCI, or make terminal-TF claims.

review_locator: PMID:33171667, Phoenixin: More than Reproductive Peptide; GPR173 section
primary_title: Phoenixin Activates Immortalized GnRH and Kisspeptin Neurons Through the Novel Receptor GPR173; Hypothalamic action of phoenixin to control reproductive hormone secretion in females: importance of the orphan G protein-coupled receptor Gpr173
decision_basis: The review identifies GPR173 as the proposed phoenixin receptor and cites two primary studies; PNX-dependent cAMP/PKA/CREB and reproductive-neuroendocrine outputs are lost or reduced after GPR173 knockdown in hypothalamic and pituitary models and in vivo rat experiments.
limitations_preserved: Record as receptor-dependent activation/function rather than direct ligand occupancy: preserve PNX-20 amide, GPR173 knockdown and hypothalamic/pituitary rat or immortalized-neuron context; the cognate physical binding interface and exact G-protein subtype remain unresolved, and no SCI or terminal-TF inference is made.

review_locator: PMID:37321907, Glycine: a long-sought novel ligand for GPR158; review discussion; PMCID:PMC10953447, Orphan peptide and G protein-coupled receptor signalling in alcohol use disorder, GPR158 section
primary_title: Orphan receptor GPR158 serves as a metabotropic glycine receptor: mGlyR
decision_basis: The reviews identify GPR158 as the proposed metabotropic glycine receptor and cite the primary structural and functional study; glycine directly binds the extracellular Cache domain, modulates the receptor-associated RGS7-Gbeta5 complex, lowers cAMP, and regulates neuronal excitability in cortical neurons.
limitations_preserved: Preserve GPR158 as a noncanonical class-C receptor and glycine as a Cache-domain ligand that modulates the receptor-associated RGS7-Gbeta5 complex; taurine is a related modulator, glycine is not a claim of canonical G-protein agonism, and no universal metabotropic glycine-receptor, SCI or terminal-TF inference is made.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC13494238, IUPHAR CXXII orphan-GPCR evaluation, GPR31 section
primary_title: The pyruvate-GPR31 axis promotes transepithelial dendrite formation in human intestinal dendritic cells; GPR31-dependent dendrite protrusion of intestinal CX3CR1+ cells by bacterial metabolites; Pyruvate enhances oral tolerance via GPR31
decision_basis: The review identifies pyruvate as a GPR31 stimulus and cites primary mouse and human intestinal studies; pyruvate produces GPR31-dependent dendrite extension in intestinal CX3CR1-high myeloid cells and human cDC1s, with downstream antigen uptake/oral-tolerance effects.
limitations_preserved: Preserve pyruvate as a gut microbial metabolite and GPR31/12-HETER as the receptor context; primary evidence is receptor-dependent cellular activation/function rather than a purified pyruvate-GPR31 occupancy assay, and no universal G-protein mechanism, SCI or terminal-TF inference is made.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC13494238, IUPHAR CXXII orphan-GPCR evaluation, GPR31 section
primary_title: GPR31-dependent dendrite protrusion of intestinal CX3CR1+ cells by bacterial metabolites; Pyruvate enhances oral tolerance via GPR31
decision_basis: The review identifies lactate as a reported GPR31 stimulus and cites the primary intestinal studies; bacterial lactate induces GPR31-dependent dendrite protrusion in mouse intestinal CX3CR1-positive cells and contributes to downstream immune/oral-tolerance phenotypes.
limitations_preserved: Preserve lactate as a bacterial metabolite and GPR31/12-HETER as the receptor context; evidence is GPR31-dependent cellular function without purified lactate-receptor binding or a universal G-protein assignment, and no SCI or terminal-TF inference is made.

review_locator: PMID:37732646; PMCID:PMC10586760; DOI:10.1042/BCJ20220309, Chemical biology tools for protein labelling: insights into cell–cell communication; interaction-guided/photoaffinity receptor-discovery section
primary_title: Deciphering intercellular signaling complexes by interaction-guided chemical proteomics
decision_basis: The method review describes interaction-guided/photoaffinity proteomics for identifying target receptors in cell-cell communication and cites Zheng et al. 2023; the cited primary supplies the exact PLAU-NRP1 interaction and NRP1-dependent ERK/proliferation evidence.
limitations_preserved: Preserve secreted PLAU/pro-uPA form, pancreatic cancer-to-stellate-cell paracrine context and NRP1 as a non-kinase co-receptor; no MET/VEGFR substitution, broad uPA signaling, SCI/terminal-TF inference, or claim that the method review itself independently established the pair.

review_locator: PMID:23230437, Annexin A1 and its receptors in inflammation; the review identifies FPR1/FPR2 receptor usage
primary_title: A novel ligand of the formyl peptide receptor: annexin I regulates neutrophil extravasation by interacting with the FPR
decision_basis: The review nominates FPR1 as an Annexin A1 receptor and cites the primary study; the primary supports N-terminal Annexin I peptide interaction with FPR-family receptor systems and FPR1-linked neutrophil responses.
limitations_preserved: Preserve the N-terminal Annexin A1 peptide/mature-protein form and FPR1-versus-FPR2, dose-dependent biased-response boundaries; primary neutrophil and receptor-system evidence does not establish a universal FPR1 route, SCI context or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6784047, beta-defensin receptor discussion; the review identifies CCR2 as a receptor candidate for hBD3 migration
primary_title: Human beta-defensin 2 and 3 and their mouse orthologs induce chemotaxis through interaction with CCR2
decision_basis: The review nominates CCR2 for hBD3-mediated leukocyte migration and cites the primary study; the primary demonstrates hBD3-Fc binding to CCR2-transfected HEK293 cells, dose-dependent CCR2-specific chemotaxis and loss of mouse peritoneal-cell migration in CCR2-deficient cells.
limitations_preserved: Preserve hBD3 disulfide/Fc-fusion and species/assay context; CCR2-dependent chemotaxis is not evidence for CCR6 substitution, a universal G-protein route, SCI transfer or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3135719, Melanocortin control of energy balance, AGRP receptor-pharmacology discussion
primary_title: Characterization of Agouti-related protein binding to melanocortin receptors
decision_basis: The review identifies AGRP as an endogenous melanocortin antagonist and cites the primary receptor-pharmacology study; the primary shows radiolabeled AGRP(87-132) binding to cloned MC3R and dose-dependent inhibition of alpha-MSH-generated cAMP at melanocortin receptors.
limitations_preserved: Preserve AGRP(87-132)/mature AGRP fragment and competitive-antagonist/inverse-agonist semantics; cloned-receptor pharmacology does not establish a universal physiological coupling route, SCI context or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3135719, Melanocortin control of energy balance, AGRP receptor-pharmacology discussion
primary_title: Characterization of Agouti-related protein binding to melanocortin receptors
decision_basis: The review identifies AGRP as an endogenous melanocortin antagonist and cites the primary receptor-pharmacology study; the primary shows radiolabeled AGRP(87-132) binding to cloned MC5R and dose-dependent inhibition of alpha-MSH-generated cAMP at melanocortin receptors.
limitations_preserved: Preserve AGRP(87-132)/mature AGRP fragment and competitive-antagonist/inverse-agonist semantics; cloned-receptor pharmacology does not establish a universal physiological coupling route, SCI context or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6155412, The Formyl Peptide Receptors: Diversity of Ligands and Mechanism for Recognition; PMCID:PMC9545948, FPR2 IUPHAR review
primary_title: LL-37, the neutrophil granule- and epithelial cell-derived cathelicidin, utilizes formyl peptide receptor-like 1 (FPRL1) as a receptor to chemoattract human peripheral blood neutrophils, monocytes, and T cells
decision_basis: The reviews identify LL-37 as an FPR2/FPRL1 agonist and cite the primary chemotaxis study; the primary reports FPRL1-dependent chemoattraction of human neutrophils, monocytes and T cells by LL-37.
limitations_preserved: Preserve LL-37 mature cathelicidin form and FPRL1=FPR2/ALX nomenclature; primary supports receptor-mediated chemotaxis rather than purified direct binding or a universal coupling route, with no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8105286, Biophysics of Notch Signaling, ligand-receptor binding/structural basis section
primary_title: The ectodomains determine ligand function in vivo and selectivity of DLL1 and DLL4 toward NOTCH1 and NOTCH2 in vitro
decision_basis: The review identifies DLL4 as a canonical Notch ligand and cites the primary selectivity study; the primary shows cell-based and biochemical evidence that DLL4 preferentially activates NOTCH1 over NOTCH2, with ectodomain determinants of ligand function.
limitations_preserved: Preserve membrane/ectodomain-dependent juxtacrine DLL4-Notch1 activation and NOTCH1 preference over NOTCH2; cell-based activation and developmental comparator evidence do not imply a universal SCI receiver state or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3113299, Similarities and differences in structure, expression, and functions of VLDLR and ApoER2, ApoE-binding discussion
primary_title: Domains of apoE required for binding to apoE receptor 2 and to phospholipids: implications for the functions of apoE in the brain
decision_basis: The review identifies ApoER2/LRP8 as an ApoE-binding LDL-receptor-family member and cites the primary binding study; the primary demonstrates specific binding of reconstituted POPC-ApoE particles and multiple ApoE isoforms/fragments to ApoER2-expressing cells.
limitations_preserved: Preserve ApoE isoform, lipidated/reconstituted particle and ApoER2/LRP8 receptor context; the primary supports binding/uptake-relevant receptor recognition, not a universal intracellular relay, SCI effect or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8193087, Selenium Transport Mechanism via Selenoprotein P, ApoER2 section
primary_title: Isoform-specific Binding of Selenoprotein P to the beta-Propeller Domain of Apolipoprotein E Receptor 2 Mediates Selenium Supply
decision_basis: The review identifies ApoER2 as a Selenoprotein P receptor and cites the primary isoform-mechanism study; the primary shows that longer Selenoprotein P isoforms bind the ApoER2 YWTD beta-propeller domain and mediate receptor-dependent selenium supply/uptake.
limitations_preserved: Preserve long Selenoprotein P isoforms with six or more selenocysteines and the ApoER2 YWTD beta-propeller binding site; uptake/selenium supply is not evidence for a canonical kinase relay, SCI effect or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7072043, Megalin: a Novel Determinant of Renin-Angiotensin System Activity in the Kidney?, megalin/AngII section
primary_title: Megalin binds and internalizes angiotensin II
decision_basis: The review identifies megalin/LRP2 as an AngII uptake receptor and cites the primary study; the primary reports direct binding of purified megalin to AngII by SPR and megalin-dependent AngII uptake in cells and mouse proximal-tubule membrane preparations.
limitations_preserved: Preserve AngII as the tested peptide ligand and megalin/LRP2 endocytic receptor context; do not conflate this with AT1R signaling or infer a canonical kinase relay, SCI effect or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7306921, Sorting Out the Role of the Sortilin-Related Receptor 1 in Alzheimer’s Disease, ApoE/SORL1 section
primary_title: Activation and functional characterization of the mosaic receptor SorLA/LR11

decision_basis: The reviews identify CD7 as a cognate SECTM1 receptor; the cited human and murine primary studies show SECTM1 binding to CD7 with PI3K-linked monocyte migration or T-cell costimulation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve soluble versus membrane SECTM1 isoforms, human CD7-dependent versus murine alternative-receptor semantics, and immune-cell context; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4839075; PMCID:PMC5837762
primary_title: Human Secreted Ly-6/uPAR Related Protein-1 (SLURP-1) Is a Selective Allosteric Antagonist of alpha7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor
decision_basis: The review identifies SLURP1 as an alpha7 nicotinic-receptor ligand; the cited primary demonstrates selective allosteric binding/inhibition and CHRNA7-dependent cellular effects.
limitations_preserved: Preserve SLURP1 as an allosteric modulator rather than an orthosteric agonist, with CHRNA7/CHRFAM7A and cell-context boundaries; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMID:23303343; PMCID:PMC3954031
primary_title: MUC1 mucin core protein binds to the domain 1 of ICAM-1; MUC1 initiates a calcium signal after ligation by intercellular adhesion molecule-1
decision_basis: The reviews identify the MUC1 tandem-repeat ectodomain as an ICAM-1 ligand; cited primary studies map MUC1 binding to ICAM-1 domain 1 and show calcium signaling, adhesion and transendothelial migration.
limitations_preserved: Preserve underglycosylated MUC1 VNTR/tandem-repeat form and ICAM-1 domain-1 heterotypic adhesion context; signaling is a bounded tumor-cell calcium/migration readout, not a universal MUC1 relay or SCI/terminal-TF claim.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3389612; PMCID:PMC8093976
primary_title: Complexes of plexin-A4 and plexin-D1 convey semaphorin-3C signals to induce cytoskeletal collapse in the absence of neuropilins
decision_basis: The reviews describe class-3 semaphorin receptor complexes containing Plexin-D1; the cited primary shows SEMA3C-dependent cytoskeletal collapse and repulsion through a Plexin-D1/Plexin-A4 complex, enhanced by neuropilins but retained after neuropilin knockout.
limitations_preserved: Preserve secreted SEMA3C, Plexin-D1/Plexin-A4 complex and neuropilin-enhancement/knockout boundary; do not infer a direct SEMA3C-TREM2 or NRP-independent universal pathway, SCI or terminal-TF effect.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC5160034; PMCID:PMC4938514; PMCID:PMC11108563
primary_title: Semaphorin 6B acts as a receptor in post-crossing commissural axon guidance
decision_basis: The reviews identify class-6 semaphorin reverse-receptor interactions; the cited primary demonstrates that Sema6B binds floorplate-derived Plexin-A2 and functions as a receptor in post-crossing commissural axon guidance.
limitations_preserved: Preserve bidirectional semaphorin/plexin semantics: Sema6B acts as the axonal receptor and Plexin-A2 is the floorplate-derived ligand, with possible cis interaction; do not encode a canonical one-way ligand claim or infer SCI-injury/terminal-TF effects.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC1569539; PMCID:PMC3366695
primary_title: Class IV semaphorin Sema4A enhances T-cell activation and interacts with Tim-2
decision_basis: The reviews identify Tim-2 as a Sema4A receptor; the cited primary identifies Tim-2 by expression cloning, demonstrates Sema4A-Fc binding and receptor phosphorylation, and reports T-cell activation and EAE modulation.
limitations_preserved: Preserve mouse Tim-2, which lacks a direct human ortholog, as an immune receptor context; Tim-2 is not necessarily the sole Sema4A receptor, and no SCI or terminal-TF inference is made.

review_locator: PMID:34778273; PMCID:PMC7492727
primary_title: The collagen ColQ binds to LRP4 and regulates the activation of the Muscle-Specific Kinase-LRP4 receptor complex by agrin at the neuromuscular junction
decision_basis: The reviews place ColQ in the agrin-LRP4-MuSK neuromuscular-junction complex; the cited primary demonstrates direct ColQ binding to LRP4 and indirect MuSK association, with competition against agrin and modulation of agrin-induced MuSK-LRP4 signaling.
limitations_preserved: Preserve ColQ as an AChE-associated extracellular matrix ligand/regulator and LRP4 as the agrin/MuSK coreceptor; direct ColQ-MuSK binding was not supported, and no SCI or canonical growth-factor inference is made.

primary_title: Crystal structure of the soluble human 55 kd TNF receptor-human TNF beta complex: implications for TNF receptor activation
decision_basis: The reviews place soluble lymphotoxin-alpha in the TNF ligand-receptor system; the cited primary resolves the soluble human 55-kDa TNF receptor/TNF-beta complex and shows trimeric LTalpha engaging three receptor molecules.
limitations_preserved: Restrict to direct soluble LTalpha3-TNFR1 complex assembly; distinguish secreted LTalpha3 from membrane LTalpha1beta2-LTBR signaling, and do not infer a full-cell downstream or SCI/terminal-TF effect.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3789601; PMCID:PMC13100631
primary_title: PTPσ Drives Excitatory Presynaptic Assembly via Various Extracellular and Intracellular Mechanisms
decision_basis: The reviews identify Slitrks as extracellular ligands for LAR-RPTPs; the cited primary shows that extracellular PTPσ-Slitrk interactions are required for Slitrk6-induced heterologous excitatory presynaptic assembly and that neuronal PTPσ or downstream-substrate perturbation suppresses the phenotype.
limitations_preserved: Promote the extracellular-interaction-dependent Slitrk6-PTPσ adhesion/synaptogenesis layer without claiming purified binary affinity or direct PTPσ-substrate binding; preserve PTPσ splice and neuronal-development context, with no SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMID:36863658, The endocytosis receptor megalin: From bench to bedside; PMCID:PMC5512543, Receptor-Mediated Endocytosis in the Proximal Tubule
primary_title: Megalin/gp330 mediates uptake of albumin in renal proximal tubule

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7461916, Reciprocal Interplay Between Fibrillar Collagens and Collagen-Binding Integrins; PMCID:PMC7960628, Integrin α11β1 is a receptor for collagen XIII
primary_title: alpha11beta1 integrin is a receptor for interstitial collagens involved in cell migration and collagen reorganization on mesenchymal nonmuscle cells
decision_basis: The reviews identify alpha11beta1 as a collagen-I receptor; the cited primary shows that human alpha11 expression in collagen-receptor-deficient mouse C2C12 cells confers preferential adhesion to collagen I, focal contacts, collagen-gel contraction and migration on collagen I.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10451079, Lipocalin 2 receptors: facts, fictions, and myths; PMCID:PMC5512543, Receptor-Mediated Endocytosis in the Proximal Tubule
primary_title: The endocytic receptor megalin binds the iron transporting neutrophil-gelatinase-associated lipocalin with high affinity and mediates its cellular uptake.
decision_basis: The reviews identify LRP2/megalin as an endocytic receptor for LCN2/NGAL; the cited primary demonstrates high-affinity human NGAL–megalin binding by SPR and antibody-blocked uptake in a megalin-expressing rat yolk-sac cell line.
limitations_preserved: Promote only LCN2/NGAL-to-LRP2/megalin binding and endocytic uptake; preserve high-affinity SPR and rat epithelial context, distinguish SLC22A17/24p3R, and do not infer kinase relay, SCI or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3713533, Structure-function and regulation of ADAMTS13 protease; PMCID:PMC5814862, ADAMTS-13 and von Willebrand factor: a dynamic duo
primary_title: ADAMTS13 binds to CD36: a potential mechanism for platelet and endothelial localization of ADAMTS13.
decision_basis: The reviews identify the C-terminal thrombospondin repeats of ADAMTS13 as candidates for CD36-dependent cell-surface localization; the cited primary demonstrates dose-dependent binding of recombinant ADAMTS13 to recombinant CD36 and CD36-positive platelet membrane fragments while retaining protease activity.
limitations_preserved: Promote ADAMTS13–CD36 binding/localization only; preserve the C-terminal thrombospondin-repeat and platelet/endothelial context, note that the primary is in vitro and retains ADAMTS13 activity, and do not infer CD36 signaling, VWF cleavage enhancement, SCI or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMID:23237509, Immune functions of serum amyloid A; PMCID:PMC10311072, Serum amyloid A and metabolic disease: evidence for a critical role in chronic inflammatory conditions
primary_title: CD36 Is a Novel Serum Amyloid A (SAA) Receptor Mediating SAA Binding and SAA-induced Signaling in Human and Rodent Cells
decision_basis: The reviews identify CD36 among cell-surface receptors mediating SAA activity; the cited primary demonstrates CD36-dependent SAA uptake, saturable binding, cytokine induction and MAPK activation in human and rodent cell systems with CD36 loss-of-function controls.
limitations_preserved: Promote SAA1-to-CD36 binding and bounded inflammatory signaling/function; preserve SAA oligomer/lipid/HDL and species/cell-context caveats, distinguish TLR/FPRL1 co-receptors, and do not infer a universal CD36-only relay, SCI or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3398014, L1CAM Binds ErbB Receptors through Ig-Like Domains Coupling Cell Adhesion and Neuregulin Signalling; PMCID:PMC7291284, Different Shades of L1CAM

limitations_preserved: Preserve L1CAM Ig-like extracellular-domain and cis-association context; the primary supports physical association, not autonomous ERBB2 activation, SCI or terminal-TF inference.

primary_title: L1CAM binds ErbB receptors through Ig-like domains coupling cell adhesion and neuregulin signalling

limitations_preserved: Preserve L1CAM Ig-like extracellular-domain and cis-association context; the primary supports physical association and neuregulin sensitization, not L1CAM-alone ERBB3 activation, SCI or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC2712882, Lacritin and Other New Proteins of the Lacrimal Functional Unit; PMCID:PMC2955988, Focus on Molecules: Syndecan-1
primary_title: Heparanase deglycanation of syndecan-1 is required for binding of the epithelial-restricted prosecretory mitogen lacritin

review_locator: PMCID:PMC3899539, Angiopoietin-Like Proteins: A Comprehensive Look; PMCID:PMC3367397, Inhibitory receptors bind ANGPTLs and support blood stem cells and leukaemia development
primary_title: Inhibitory receptors bind ANGPTLs and support blood stem cells and leukaemia development

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6784047, beta-Defensins: Multifunctional Modulators of Infection, Inflammation and More
primary_title: Human beta-defensin 2 and 3 and their mouse orthologs induce chemotaxis through interaction with CCR2

limitations_preserved: Preserve mature hBD3 fusion/peptide and CCR2-dependent myeloid chemotaxis context; hBD3 also has CCR6-independent activities, so do not claim CCR2 exclusivity or SCI/terminal-TF effects.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4394689, International Union of Basic and Clinical Pharmacology. XCV. Recent Advances in the Understanding of the Pharmacology and Biological Roles of Relaxin Family Peptide Receptors 1–4
primary_title: Multiple binding sites revealed by interaction of relaxin family peptides with native and chimeric relaxin family peptide receptors 1 and 2 (LGR7 and LGR8)
decision_basis: The review describes relaxin-family peptide binding and activation at RXFP2/LGR8 and cites the primary receptor-chimera study showing relaxin-family peptide binding-site and cAMP signaling behavior at RXFP2.
limitations_preserved: Preserve relaxin-2/relaxin-family peptide, receptor species and two-stage ectodomain/transmembrane-site model; RXFP2 binding is species- and peptide-dependent and may be low-efficiency/partial, so do not equate it with the canonical INSL3-RXFP2 or Relaxin-RXFP1 edges.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC6028831, SCARF1: a multifaceted, yet largely understudied, scavenger receptor
primary_title: SREC-I, a type F scavenger receptor, is an endocytic receptor for calreticulin
decision_basis: The review identifies calreticulin as a SCARF1/SREC-I ligand and cites the primary study showing SREC-I-dependent calreticulin recognition and endocytic uptake.
limitations_preserved: Preserve surface/extracellular calreticulin cargo and SREC-I/SCARF1 scavenger-receptor topology; uptake/cross-presentation context only; do not infer canonical signaling, SCI, or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMID:39930176, MFRP in Early Onset Retinal Degeneration: Clinical and Molecular Perspectives
primary_title: Disease mechanisms in late-onset retinal macular degeneration associated with mutation in C1QTNF5
decision_basis: The MFRP review identifies the C1QTNF5/CTRP5 interaction and cites the primary study reporting yeast two-hybrid, pull-down, co-immunoprecipitation and RPE co-localization evidence.
limitations_preserved: Preserve secreted C1QTNF5/CTRP5 and type-II membrane MFRP in the retinal/RPE association context; do not infer canonical receptor relay, MFRP signaling, SCI, or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMID:12676166, Bradykinin, angiotensin-(1-7), and ACE inhibitors: how do they interact?
primary_title: Human ACE and bradykinin B2 receptors form a complex at the plasma membrane
decision_basis: The review discusses ACE–B2-receptor cross-talk and cites the primary study demonstrating a plasma-membrane ACE/B2R complex with co-immunoprecipitation, FRET and bradykinin-induced cointernalization.
limitations_preserved: ACE is an ectoenzyme/partner, not a B2R ligand; preserve heteromer/crosstalk and ACE-inhibitor modulation semantics, with no autonomous ACE-to-B2R signaling, SCI, or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC11364484, Emerging role of BMPs/BMPR2 signaling pathway in treatment for pulmonary fibrosis; PMCID:PMC7502536, Structural Perspective of BMP ligands and Signaling
primary_title: Specificity and Structure of a High Affinity Activin Receptor-like Kinase 1 (ALK1) Signaling Complex
decision_basis: The reviews identify BMP10 as a ligand for the type-II receptor ACVR2A/ActRIIA and cite primary receptor-binding work.
limitations_preserved: Promote direct BMP10–ACVR2A type-II receptor binding only; preserve non-exclusive ACVR2A/ACVR2B/BMPR2 usage and soluble ectodomain context, with no complete type-I holocomplex, SCI, or terminal-TF inference.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC7355470, Selectins; PMCID:PMC1867022, Endothelial ligands for L-selectin
primary_title: Not just a marker: CD34 on human hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells dominates vascular selectin binding along with CD44
decision_basis: The selectin reviews identify CD34-family sialomucins as vascular selectin ligands and cite primary evidence that CD34 on human hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells contributes P-selectin binding and rolling adhesion.
limitations_preserved: Promote CD34 glycoform–P-selectin binding/adhesion only; preserve O-glycan/sialofucosylation and flow context, and do not infer intracellular relay, CD34 receptor autonomy, SCI, or terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4382859, Role of syndecan-2 in osteoblast biology and pathology; PMCID:PMC1218755, Syndecans: multifunctional cell-surface co-receptors
primary_title: Syndecan-2 is involved in the mitogenic activity and signaling of granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor in osteoblasts

limitations_preserved: Promote GM-CSF–SDC2 binding/co-receptor modulation with GM-CSF-receptor-alpha cooperation and osteoblast ERK/mitogenic function; preserve heparan-sulfate dependence and do not treat SDC2 as the canonical signaling receptor or infer SCI/terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC4624607, Endostatin's Emerging Roles in Angiogenesis, Lymphangiogenesis, Disease, and Clinical Applications; PMCID:PMC3270378, Cellular Actions and Signaling by Endostatin
primary_title: Cell surface glypicans are low-affinity endostatin receptors
decision_basis: The endostatin reviews identify glypican-1 heparan-sulfate chains as low-affinity surface binding partners/co-receptors and cite expression-cloning, biochemical, glycan-dependence, and antisense functional evidence.
limitations_preserved: Promote low-affinity endostatin–GPC1 heparan-sulfate binding/co-receptor function only; preserve the proposed two-receptor/unknown high-affinity receptor model and do not infer a standalone GPC1 signaling relay or SCI/terminal-TF activity.

review_locator: PMCID:PMC10696404, The universe of galectin-binding partners and their functions in health and disease; PMCID:PMC8464943, Galectins in endothelial biology
primary_title: Galectin-8 interacts with podoplanin and modulates lymphatic endothelial cell functions

review_locator: PMCID:PMC8642587, CCN2 interactome; PMCID:PMC2721079, Connective tissue growth factor CCN2 in diabetic nephropathy
primary_title: Connective tissue growth factor CCN2 interacts with and activates the tyrosine kinase receptor TrkA
